content: Never back up SQLite by copying the file with cp (not transactionally safe, risk of corruption mid-write). Use sqlite3's built-in .backup command or 'VACUUM INTO' (single-transaction snapshot, good under write load) via a cron script, then compress and copy off-device (e.g., rclone to cloud, or scp to another machine) — backups must leave the Pi/SD card to survive card failure. Litestream is a lightweight continuous-replication alternative (streams WAL to S3/local) but adds a background process; for a single-user low-write app, a simple nightly cron + VACUUM INTO + off-device copy is sufficient and lower-maintenance.
